# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

content:
Fixed. The issue was in `textkit/slug.py`: the regex `[^a-z0-9]` replaced each non-alphanumeric character individually with a hyphen, so consecutive punctuation/spaces produced multiple hyphens, and leading/trailing characters produced leading/trailing hyphens.

The fix:
- Changed the pattern to `[^a-z0-9]+` so runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen.
- Added `.strip("-")` to remove any leading/trailing hyphens.

Verified: `slugify("Hello,  World!")` → `"hello-world"`, `slugify("--a--b--")` → `"a-b"`, and the test suite passes. The public signature is unchanged.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` (collapsing consecutive non-alphanumeric characters into a single hyphen) and adding `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. Public signature unchanged; both issue examples now produce the expected output and the test suite passes.
